transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've reviewed the eighth-grade civics class proposal for the local oral-history project. Before I can approve this, I need to make sure we have a complete approval packet as required by district policy. Specifically, I'll need current findings from our project advisor, school counselor, and instructional technology coordinator covering student eligibility, consent, recording technology, storage, and retention. I'd like to hear from each of you on these matters so we can determine whether this project is ready to move forward or whether adjustments need to be made to the draft plan.

transcript.text: I've completed a roster review, and I need to share an important finding regarding student eligibility. Exactly eight students have completed the district's media-ethics training: J1, J3, J6, J8, J11, J14, J17, and J20. Only those eight students may conduct recorded interviews. Additionally, the approval file must include a training-verification record documenting this. This means the draft plan, which calls for all 20 students to conduct interviews, will need to be adjusted accordingly.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I've completed my family-consent review, and I have an important finding regarding consent for public publication. Five interviewees — I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 — have not granted permission for public web publication. Their recordings may be used only in the school's internal archive. The other 15 interviewees may be included in public publication. The approval plan must include a consent-exclusion record documenting this. This means the draft plan, which calls for publishing all 20 recordings on the public school website, will need to be adjusted so that only the 15 consented recordings are published publicly.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I've completed my technology review, and I have several important findings regarding recording technology, storage, and retention. First, personal phones cannot be used for school recordings — the project must use district tablets instead. Second, all source files must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive, not on personal devices or general school storage. Third, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation — they cannot be retained indefinitely as the draft plan currently calls for. Finally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record documenting these arrangements. This means the draft plan will need to be adjusted on all three counts: recording devices, storage location, and retention timeline.
